title: Osero's Pioneer Incentive Pool is not a segregated account — it is the Agent's own SubProxy address
content:
A.6.1.1.7.2.5.3.2.1.1.2.1 states that "the address of Osero's Pioneer Incentive Pool is Osero's SubProxy Account on the Ethereum Mainnet" — and gives the same address recorded as the SubProxy in the Agent Creation parameters (A.6.1.1.7.2.1.1.3.1.1.2).

The Pool is therefore a designation, not a container. Nothing in the Artifact separates incentive-pool funds from the Agent's general holdings; the two are the same balance under two names.

That collides with another rule in the same Artifact. A.6.1.1.7.2.3.2.2.1.2.1.1 requires Osero to keep *all* tokens of other Agents in its SubProxy account, because the Upkeep Rebate is computed from those holdings and Operational GovOps verifies the calculation against them. The address that must be readable as "the rebate base" is now also "the Pioneer Incentive Pool," and by default "everything else Osero holds."

The consequence is that address-level observability, which the rebate protocol relies on, does not by itself distinguish committed incentive funds from rebate-eligible holdings. An observer can see the total but not the earmarks, so any separation between the two mandates has to be maintained off-chain in the accounting rather than on-chain in the custody.

This is a tension rather than a contradiction — nothing in the text is violated — but it weakens the verification story that made the single-custody rule attractive in the first place.
description: The same address holds peer-Agent tokens for the upkeep rebate and the incentive pool, so two mandates with different beneficiaries share one balance.
